questions.q: The electronic configuration of elements $A, B$ and $C$ are $[\mathrm{He}] 2 s^1,[\mathrm{Ne}] 3 s^1$ and [Ar] $4 s^1$ respectively, which one of the following order is correct for the first ionization potentials (in $\mathrm{kJ} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ) of $A, B$ and $C$ ?
questions.solution:
Ionisation potential of $A, B$ and $C$ elements decreases with the ease of removal of electron from $A$ to $C$. Atomic size increase from $A$ to $C$, hence ionisation potential decrease in the same order.
So, order of ionisation potential is $A > B > C$

questions.q: In graph of atomic volume versus atomic weight, the elements corresponding to peaks in the curve belong to
questions.solution:
If we see the atomic mass versus atomic volume curve, we will notice the following features:

  • Alkali metals such as $\text{Na,}\text{K,}\text{Rb}$ which have similar properties occur as peaks of the curve.
  • Halogen elements like $\text{F,}\text{Cl,}\text{Br,}$ which have similar properties occur at the rising or the ascending part of the curve.
  • Noble gases such as $\text{Ne,}\text{Ar,}\text{Kr}$ which have similar properties occur just before the alkali elements.
  • Hydrogen and Helium seem to be exception to the rule.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: The correct decreasing order of negative electron gain enthalpy for $\mathrm{C}, \mathrm{Ca}, \mathrm{Al}, \mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrm{O}$ is
questions.solution:
The electron gain enthalpy is the energy released when an electron is added to a neutral gaseous atom. Generally, it becomes more negative (higher magnitude) across a period from left to right and decreases down a group.

The elements given are $\mathrm{F}$ (Group 17, Period 2), $\mathrm{O}$ (Group 16, Period 2), $\mathrm{C}$ (Group 14, Period 2), $\mathrm{Al}$ (Group 13, Period 3), and $\mathrm{Ca}$ (Group 2, Period 4).

Comparing the magnitudes of electron gain enthalpy:
1. $\mathrm{F}$ has the highest negative electron gain enthalpy among these due to its small size and high effective nuclear charge, although it is slightly less than $\mathrm{Cl}$ due to inter-electronic repulsion.
2. $\mathrm{O}$ follows $\mathrm{F}$ in the same period.
3. $\mathrm{C}$ has a lower negative electron gain enthalpy than $\mathrm{O}$.
4. $\mathrm{Al}$ is a metal with a low tendency to gain electrons, but it is more electronegative than $\mathrm{Ca}$.
5. $\mathrm{Ca}$ is an alkaline earth metal with a stable $ns^2$ configuration, making its electron gain enthalpy very low (near zero or positive).

The order of magnitude of negative electron gain enthalpy is $\mathrm{F} > \mathrm{O} > \mathrm{C} > \mathrm{Al} > \mathrm{Ca}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{F}> \mathrm{O}> \mathrm{C}> \mathrm{Al}> \mathrm{Ca}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Which from following is a CORRECT decreasing order of ionisation enthalpy for different elements?
questions.solution:
The ionisation enthalpy decreases down the group due to increase in the atomic size.
Therefore, ionisation enthalpy of $\mathrm{Ne}$ is more than that of Ar.
Across a period ionisation enthalpy increases with increase of atomic number.
Therefore, ionisation enthalpy of $\mathrm{S}, \mathrm{Cl}$ and $\mathrm{Ar}$ is in the order: $\mathrm{S} < \mathrm{Cl} < \mathrm{Ar}$.
Hence, the correct decreasing order of ionisation enthalpy for the given elements is:
$\mathrm{Ne} > \mathrm{Ar} > \mathrm{Cl} > \mathrm{S}$

The atomic numbers of elements $A, B, C$ and $D$ are $Z-1, Z, Z+1$ and $Z+2$, respectively. If ' $B$ ' is a noble gas, choose the correct answers from the following statements
(1) ' $A$ ' has higher electron affinity
(2) ' $C$ ' exists in +2 oxidation state
(3) ' $D$ ' is an alkaline earth metal

Given,
Atomic number of element $B=Z$
(\because$ noble gas \quad \therefore$ belong to zero group)
Atomic number of element $A=Z-1$
(ie, halogens)
Atomic number of element $C=Z+1$
(ie, group IA)
Atomic number of element $D=Z+2$
(ie, group IIA)
$\because$ Element $B$ is a noble gas
$\therefore$ Element $A$ must be a halogen ie, have highest electron affinity.
and element $C$ must be an alkali metal and exist in +1 oxidation state.
and element $D$ must be an alkaline earth metal with +2 oxidation state.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: $In the following sets of reactants which two sets best exhibit the amphoteric character of Al_{2}O_{3}. xH_{2}O ? \begin{cases}\text{Set I} & {Al}_{2} {O}_{3} \cdot {xH}_{2} \text{O} \left(\text{s}\right) + {OH}_{\text{aq}^{-} \\ \text{Set II} & {Al}_{2} {O}_{3} \text{x} \cdot {H}_{2} \text{O} \left(\text{s}\right) + {H}_{2} \text{O} \left(\text{l}\right) \\ \text{Set III} & {Al}_{2} {O}_{3} \text{x} \cdot {H}_{2} \text{O} \left(\text{s}\right) + {H}_{\text{aq}^{+} \\ \text{Set IV} & {Al}_{2} {O}_{3} \cdot {xH}_{2} \text{O} \left(\text{s}\right) + {NH}_{3 \left(\text{aq}\right)}\end{cases}$
questions.solution: For a substance to be called amphoteric, it should be able to react as a base as well as an acid. Hence, when it is reacted with a base, it should act as an acid, and when it is reacted with an acid, it should behave as a base. The reactions for amphoteric nature of Al_{2}O_{3}. x H_{2}O(s) are ${Al}_{2} {O}_{3}. x {H}_{2} \text{O} \left(\text{s}\right) \overset{\text{OH} \text{aq} -}{→} \text{Al} {\left(\text{OH}\right)}_{4}^{-} aq$ & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & Aluminate anion ${Al}_{2} {O}_{3}. x {H}_{2} \text{O} \left(\text{s}\right) \overset{\text{H} \text{aq} +}{→} {\left[\text{Al} {\left({H}_{2} \text{O}\right)}_{6}\right]}_{aq}^{3 +}$. [Al(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+} is octahedral complex ion [Al(OH)_{4}]^{-1} tetrahedral at pH=13

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q:
The periodic table consists of 18 groups. An isotope of copper, on bombardment with protons, undergoes a nuclear reaction yielding element $X$ as shown below. To which group, element $X$ belongs in the periodic table?

${ }_{29}^{63} \mathrm{Cu}+{ }_{1}^{1} \mathrm{H} \rightarrow 6_{0}^{1} n+{ }_{2}^{4} \alpha+2{ }_{1}^{1} \mathrm{H}+\mathrm{X}$
questions.solution:
${ }_{29}^{63} \mathrm{Cu}+{ }_{1}^{1} \mathrm{H} \rightarrow 6{ }_{0}^{1} n+{ }_{2}^{4} \mathrm{He}+2{ }_{1}^{1} \mathrm{H}+{ }_{Z}^{A} X$

Balancing the atomic mass and atomic number

$63+1=(6 \times 1)+4+2+A \Rightarrow A=52$

$29+1=(6 \times 0)+2+2+Z \Rightarrow Z=26$

Thus ${ }_{Z}^{A} X={ }_{26}^{52} X$ or ${ }_{26}^{52} \mathrm{Fe}$

Hence, $X$ belongs to group 8 in the periodic table.
